subject: chemistry

items.q: What is the difference between ionic and covalent bonding?
items.correct: Ionic transfers electrons; covalent shares them.
items.misconception: Ionic bonds form by sharing electrons.
items.random_wrong: Covalent bonds form by transferring electrons.
items.why: Metals + non-metals transfer electrons (ionic); non-metals share electrons (covalent).

items.q: When do ionic compounds conduct electricity?
items.correct: When molten or dissolved, so the ions are free to move.
items.misconception: When solid, because the ions are packed tightly.
items.random_wrong: Never, because ions cannot carry charge.
items.why: In a solid the ions are fixed in the lattice; they only carry charge when free to move.

items.correct: They have delocalised (free) electrons that can move.
items.misconception: Their positive ions flow through the wire.
items.random_wrong: Electrons are transferred to make ions.
items.why: A sea of delocalised electrons carries the charge while the metal ions stay in place.
